title: Oncall telemetry mosaic and automated postmortem seed
creator: Samir Chen
description:
Summary: Build a compact, policy-driven "mosaic" attachment that aggregates trace snippets, relevant log slices, SLO deltas, and a seeded postmortem draft into PagerDuty/Slack incident attachments. The goal is to reduce time-to-insight for oncall while preserving PII/privacy and keeping attachment sizes under channel limits. This work enables automated postmortem creation (seeded with contextual evidence) and a lightweight reviewer flow in the Console to finalize postmortems and attach playbook suggestions.

Motivation:
- Oncall currently spends 10–25 minutes assembling evidence (traces, logs, SLO changes) for high-latency incidents.
- Incident handoffs are noisy; responders miss the minimal evidence set required to diagnose regressions.
- We want to accelerate MTTR by providing compact, prioritized evidence bundles AND a draft postmortem scaffold that engineers can edit instead of authoring from scratch.

Scope of this ticket:
- Design and implement a telemetry "mosaic" producer that runs in our incident pipeline and emits attachments to PagerDuty and Slack.
- Attachments include: top 3 trace snippets (40–120 tokens each), 2 log excerpt slices (filtered by service and error class), SLO delta snapshot, and a generated postmortem seed (markdown).
- Add a Console review flow: reviewer can expand snippets in-place, flag PII, accept or redact, and publish the seeded postmortem to the team's postmortem repo.
- Policy controls for attachment granularity and retention (team-level settings).

Non-goals:
- Full-fledged natural-language incident summarizer (out of scope — separate research initiative).
- Long-term archival storage for full traces (we link to traces in the trace store).

Privacy & legal constraints:
- Attachments must honor data classification: redact fields flagged by KMS-backed rules and respect retention TTLs.
- Default mosaic policy for external-facing incidents will omit raw log lines and provide a summarized statistic instead.

Implementation notes / design decisions:
1) Evidence selection heuristics: use weighted scoring across span error counts, latency percentiles, and span tag prominence. Picks are deterministic (seeded RNG) to ensure reproducible attachments for the same incident.
2) Compact serialization: mosaic is emitted as a small JSON blob (<= 10 KB) with preformatted markdown for Slack and PagerDuty text bodies. For Slack, we render a button to open the Console reviewer.
3) Postmortem seed template: minimal sections (summary, timeline highlights, impact, probable root cause, next steps). We auto-fill timeline with picks and include links to full artifacts.
4) Rate limiting & throttles: only attach mosaic for incidents above 'latency' or 'error' thresholds to avoid noise.
5) Fallback policy: if trace store is unavailable, include best-effort SLO snapshot and a pointer to the incident trace retrieval job.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Detail vs. size: we cap snippet length to balance usefulness and channel constraints. Some detailed traces will be truncated; we opted for multiple short snippets rather than a single long one.
- Automation vs. accuracy: automated postmortem seeds speed up workflow but risk incorrect hypotheses. To mitigate this, we surface confidence indicators and require human sign-off before publishing.

Acceptance criteria:
- Mosaic attachments are produced for >= 90% of qualifying incidents in staging and delivered to PD and Slack with correct formatting.
- Console reviewer can open a mosaic, redact fields, and publish the postmortem seed to the team repo.
- Attachment size caps are respected under 10 KB for PD and 8 KB for Slack message bodies.
- Privacy rules enforced: redacted fields match KMS-based rule set.
- Integration tests for trace-unavailable fallback pass.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): produce mosaics for incidents in observability-test org and surface reviewer flow for _oncall-dev_ only.
- Phase 2 (pilot): enable for 3 production teams with opt-in policy and gather MTTR impact metrics.
- Phase 3 (org-wide): enable by default with team-level controls and configurable thresholds.

Monitoring & metrics:
- Emit telemetry: mosaic.generated, mosaic.published, mosaic.redacted, mosaic.size_bytes, mosaic.publish_latency.
- Dashboards: new "Mosaic Attachments" Grafana panel linking to SLO and incidents list.
